title: Claim is not idempotent over an existing same-assignee assignment
description:
Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03, session 2).

`jit issue claim <id> <assignee>` hard-fails with "Issue is already assigned" even when the existing assignee IS the claimant. The assign-then-claim sequence is exactly what the (already filed) container-stewardship workaround produces: a lead runs `jit issue assign <id> agent:claude` while dependencies are still open (claim would exit 4), and later — once deps complete — wants to promote that assignment into a real claim/in_progress. That promotion step rejects, and the operator falls back to `jit issue update --state in_progress`, which loses claim semantics (lease, claims.jsonl) — the same loss the assign workaround already suffered.

This is adjacent to, but distinct from, issue eff11282 (claim couples assignment to the in_progress transition on dependency-blocked containers): eff11282 is about claim at intake time; this is about claim being non-idempotent over an existing same-assignee assignment at promotion time.

Proposal: `jit issue claim` on an issue whose assignee equals the claimant proceeds (records the lease, transitions to in_progress if unblocked) instead of erroring; a DIFFERENT existing assignee keeps failing as today.

Acceptance: assign X to issue I (deps open) -> complete deps -> claim I as X succeeds and I is in_progress with a live lease; claim I as Y (Y != X) still fails.
